title: A guide (I.4)
hookLine: find a wise guide, one in ten thousand
tomorrow: too much to fix. where do you even start?

cards: Coaches, tutors, therapists, mentors: there's a guide for almost everything now. So for the inner life, do you need a guide, or is God enough? Two books on the Catholic shelf seem to answer differently.

The Imitation of Christ, which we just closed, has the disciple pray: don't let Moses or the prophets speak to me, Lord; you speak. And Francis de Sales, early in his book, says: find a guide, one in ten thousand.

teach.b: Let the Imitation speak first. In book three, chapter two, the disciple asks God to speak to him directly. Human teachers, he says, can sound out the words, but only God can give the spirit inside them.
Its best case: no person can stand in for God, and a guide who gets too big can get in the way. Now de Sales.
He opens with young Tobias in the Bible, sent on a long journey, told to find a faithful companion. He steps outside, and there stands Raphael, an angel, though Tobias doesn't know it yet.

Anyone starting on the road of devotion, de Sales says, needs a guide too. He quotes Ecclesiasticus, in the Douay-Rheims: "A faithful friend is a strong defence: and he that hath found him, hath found a treasure."
Choose carefully, he says, one in ten thousand, full of charity, knowledge and prudence.
Then treat that guide with open honesty, and don't see a mere person, but trust God, who speaks through them. His best case: God usually helps us through people.
And the honest detail to share: the Imitation itself, back in book one, says take counsel from someone wise. Both books want God's voice. They differ on how often it comes with a human face.

how: Some Catholics meet a spiritual director, a priest, religious or trained lay person, every few weeks to talk about their prayer and life; others find guidance through confession, a mentor or a trusted friend.

o: a wise, trusted guide for your life of prayer
a person who assigns penances after confession
the priest in charge of a parish's music

games.q: two voices, one shelf — tap the pairs.

s: a spiritual director tells you what to believe
de Sales's guide is a faithful friend for the road, met with honesty and trust.
the Imitation also says to take counsel from someone wise
book one says it, even though book three asks God to speak directly.
de Sales says any willing person will do as a guide
choose one in ten thousand, he says: charity, knowledge and prudence.

games.q: your friend says she only needs God and the Bible, never another person's advice about prayer. what's the best case for her side, from the Imitation?
o: no person can stand in for God, and a guide can get in the way.
people are always wrong about God, so never listen to anyone.
advice is fine for life, but prayer is too private to discuss.
games.why: the disciple asks God to speak directly, since only God gives the spirit. still, the Imitation also says take counsel from someone wise, and de Sales says God speaks through a faithful friend.

practice: Think of someone wiser than you in faith or in life: a mentor, an elder, a friend who tells you the truth. Write them a short text asking if you could talk sometime soon, and send it or save it as a version.
Then rest a moment with the picture of Tobias stepping outside and finding someone already waiting.

wordCard.voice: Spiritual director. A wise, faithful friend who walks with someone on the road of devotion: chosen with care, trusted openly.

carryVoice: Your line: a faithful friend. A treasure, Ecclesiasticus says, for whoever finds one. That's day 1494.
